walkthroughs.body_html:
Sociological Theories & Approaches — a core area of GCSE Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Sociological Theories & Approaches brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Sociological Theories & Approaches.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who argued the family had become symmetrical in 1973?
options: Murdock
Parsons
Young and Willmott
Oakley

mcqs.q: Murdock (1949) identified how many family functions?
What is the postmodern view of identity?
options: Identity is fixed by class, gender, and ethnicity at birth.
Everyone has the same identity in postmodern society.
Men are oppressed by chivalrous laws.
Identities are fluid, fragmented, and constructed through consumption and choice.

mcqs.q: What does the chivalry thesis claim?
options: Women never commit crime.
Men are oppressed by chivalrous laws.
Women are treated more leniently by the criminal justice system.
Everyone has the same identity in postmodern society.

mcqs.q: What is a moral panic according to Cohen?
options: Everyone has the same identity in postmodern society.
Genuine widespread fear about a real, serious threat.
Religious leaders condemning immorality.
Disproportionate media reaction creating exaggerated public concern about a group or behaviour.
